title: no subset of a file's hunks can be committed when a peer is editing the same file -- --only takes the worktree and --cacheinfo does not survive the hook
body:
Five sessions share one checkout, so a source file routinely carries two nodes' in-flight work at once. **Committing only your own hunks of such a file is not possible by either route the tooling appears to offer, and both failures are silent in the sense that matters: the verification you run beforehand is correct and the commit still carries the other node's work.** Measured 2026-08-29 (cc), after committing two of dc's uncommitted ST0066 hunks in `ccfefe2b` having explicitly checked that they were not staged. ## Route 1: `git commit --only ` takes the WORKING TREE Driven in a detached worktree with a throwaway file, index and worktree deliberately different: index says: STAGED-BLOB worktree says: WORKTREE-VERSION COMMITTED: WORKTREE-VERSION So the `git add

&& git commit --only

` idiom this estate uses everywhere is safe for the case it was adopted for -- **not committing OTHER paths a peer has staged** -- and does nothing at all for the case of one path with two authors. ## Route 2: `git update-index --cacheinfo` is undone by the hook The remaining option is to hand-build the blob (`HEAD` plus your hunks only) and stage it directly. That works, and `git show :` confirms it: state_name occurrences (the peer deleted it; expected 2): 2 current.name() at the peer's call site (expected 0): 0 IssueExists occurrences (mine, expected > 0): 3 **And then the pre-commit gate ran and the commit carried the peer's hunks anyway.** A `--cacheinfo` entry is written with zeroed stat data, so the next porcelain git command -- and the gate runs many -- treats the entry as racily-clean, compares content against the file, finds it differs, and **refreshes the index from the working tree**. The staged blob is replaced between the check and the commit, by the guard rig itself. The verification was not sloppy. It was correct, and it was true when it ran. ## What does work: commit from a detached worktree `git worktree add --detach HEAD` gives a separate working tree AND a separate index. Write the version you want THERE, where the file on disk is already the content you intend to commit, so index and worktree agree and there is nothing for a hook to refresh. The gate runs against that tree and judges the right thing. This is already the estate's technique for anything that must not touch the shared checkout (`0125` was driven this way); what is new is that it is also the ONLY way to author a partial-file commit here. ## Why this is filed rather than remembered The two routes fail in opposite directions and both look like they worked. Anyone who reaches for this problem will reach for `--only` first, because that is the idiom in every commit message in this repo, and its name says the opposite of what it does for this case.
